classification.difficultyReason: Infer the cylinder height from the exact spherical fit, then compare two supplied surface-area formulas symbolically.

content.prompt: The figure at the right shows a sphere of radius $r$ fitting exactly into a cylinder. The sphere touches the cylinder at the top, bottom and curved surface. Show that the surface area of the sphere is equal to the area of the curved surface of the cylinder.

spec.description: Sphere inscribed in an upright cylinder; centre dot, radius r, circular end ellipses and dashed rear arcs.
spec.mathematics: The sphere and cylinder have radius r; the cylinder height equals the sphere diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius r is labelled; no derived height or answer is shown.

answer.short:
$S_{\text{sphere}}=4\pi r^2=S_{\text{curved cylinder}}$.

The cylinder has radius $r$ and height $2r$.
answer.worked:
The exact fit gives cylinder radius $r$ and height $2r$.
$$\begin{align*}S_{\text{sphere}}&=4\pi r^2\\S_{\text{curved cylinder}}&=2\pi r(2r)\\S_{\text{curved cylinder}}&=4\pi r^2\end{align*}$$
Therefore the sphere's surface area equals the cylinder's curved surface area.
